diagram_math_checks.justification: The schematic uses a=(0,0), b=(6,0), c=(3,4.8), p=(3,0), q=(4.5,2.4), r=(1.5,2.4). These satisfy p=(a+b)/2, q=(b+c)/2, r=(c+a)/2 exactly as Statement line 34. The four filled regions have the ordered vertices T1=[a,p,r], T2=[p,b,q], T3=[r,q,c], T4=[p,q,r] of Statement line 38 and proof 1.1.

By the supplier def-oriented-complex-triangle-and-boundary, each ordered triple traverses first-to-second, second-to-third, third-to-first. T1 contributes p→r versus T4 r→p; T2 q→p versus T4 p→q; T3 r→q versus T4 q→r. The three double-headed drawn edges encode exactly those opposite traversals, as explicitly defined by the caption. No single contour is claimed to traverse an edge both ways.

The six arrows are a→p→b, b→q→c and c→r→a. All six outer half-edges and all three interior edges are explicitly drawn, including r→a closure. They give six vertices, nine geometric edges and four bounded triangular faces. Supplier prop-reversal-and-concatenation-of-complex-line-integrals and proof 2.1 justify cancellation of each reverse pair and concatenation of the surviving outer pairs; proof 3.1 derives the integral identity without the figure.

The figure is labeled a nondegenerate schematic; the unchanged Statement and proof 3.1 retain repeated/collinear vertices. The final Remarks explicitly state the algebraic proof is independent of the picture. No nondegeneracy hypothesis or new dependency is introduced.
